purpose: Prove that the committed .gitattributes (LF rules for all text sources plus a narrow docs/planning/showstake-v2/VALIDATION.json text eol=crlf override) makes a fresh default Windows Git clone (core.autocrlf=true, path with spaces) check out ALL 11 packet files byte-for-byte equal to docs/evidence/bootstrap.json, and that pnpm verify passes in that clone. Two negative controls reproduce the exact prior drift.
method: 1. Confirmed effective Git setting core.autocrlf=true (system-level) — default Windows checkout.

2. POSITIVE: copy the full candidate tree (excl. .git/node_modules/.local), git add -A + commit with the reviewed .gitattributes (incl. VALIDATION.json eol=crlf), then git clone into a separate path with spaces; hash all 11 raw bytes; run pnpm verify.
3. NEGATIVE A: same tree but .gitattributes with the VALIDATION.json crlf override removed (old attr) -> VALIDATION.json checks out as the LF mismatch observed in t01-codex-52-review.json.
4. NEGATIVE B: the 11 packet files with NO .gitattributes (autocrlf=true) -> the 10 LF-recorded files drift to CRLF.
Stale GIT_CONFIG_* variables were cleared for every git invocation; only temp paths under .local/ were used; the worker does not commit or push.

conclusion: The committed .gitattributes (LF rules + VALIDATION.json eol=crlf) is the complete fix: a default Windows clone reproduces all 11 recorded bootstrap hashes and pnpm verify exits 0. Negative A reproduces the exact acceptance-blocking drift (VALIDATION.json a42e7687... LF) when the crlf override is absent; negative B shows the 10 LF files drift to CRLF without any attributes.
limits: Local Git/checkout proof only; no main commit/push. No historical hash or baseline/handoff byte changed. Postgres 52-check proof untouched (no code change).
